supporting_evidence.quote: Graphics revenue – The year-over-year increase in the second quarter and first half of fiscal year 2027 was driven by sales of our Blackwell architecture.

input.reasoning_summary:
The claim states that NVIDIA's Gaming revenue growth in Q2 FY2027 (quarter ended July 26, 2026) was driven by sales of Blackwell-based GeForce GPUs. This is an interpretive claim about the driver/cause of revenue growth.

Evidence E5 is from NVIDIA's 10-Q filed 2026-08-26 for the period ending 2026-07-26 (Q2 FY2027), which matches the claim's timeframe. The evidence states: "Graphics revenue – The year-over-year increase in the second quarter and first half of fiscal year 2027 was driven by sales of our Blackwell architecture."

The Graphics reportable segment includes Gaming products (as established in E1, which describes Gaming products including GeForce RTX GPUs). The filing explicitly attributes the Graphics revenue growth to "sales of our Blackwell architecture," which aligns with the claim's attribution to "Blackwell-based GeForce GPUs."

The claim is purely interpretive/causal (about what drove the growth) rather than making specific numeric assertions about revenue levels or growth rates. The evidence directly supports the stated driver of the revenue growth.
